### LOW: Opt\-in resident RAM prefix\-cache bank contradicts T\-041's 'no production RAM tier' assumption
[changelog\.d/nemotron\-super\-media\-discovery\.md:57](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/e659edc25318b0ba9bcbf95c2755eec8b4a1708f/changelog.d/nemotron-super-media-discovery.md#L57) · A-001, T-041

The changelog says \`DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE\_MEMORY=1\` opts the Nemotron Super owner into exact text prefix reuse\. It uses a resident recurrent checkpoint bank, sized from the KV grant \(\`min\(1 GiB, grant/8\)\`\), and reserved from load until retirement\. T\-041 and its mitigations say production never constructs or funds a resident\-RAM prefix cache, that DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE is the single gate, and that the only tier is encrypted SSD with HMAC names, a 30\-minute TTL and a KEK purge\. A RAM bank is a second reuse path\. It has no stated tie to the cacheSalt/account scoping, a different TTL, a different purge path, and a hit/miss TTFT oracle \(SEC\-035\) that lives only in process memory and is not covered by at\-rest encryption\. Trigger: an operator sets the variable and the provider serves multi\-account traffic\. Impact: cross\-tenant prefix\-presence inference if reuse is not keyed by the coordinator\-authored cacheSalt\. I could not verify the source, so this is a documentation/threat\-model gap and not a confirmed code flaw\. Fix: update T\-041 and TB\-007 to cover this opt\-in tier\. State that it is default\-off, that entries are keyed by cacheSalt, what the lifetime and purge are, and that it is cleared on unload\. Confirm in source that the salt is part of the lookup key\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Nemotron local text route can enable the prefix cache with an empty, non\-coordinator cache scope
[provider\-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/Bridge/NemotronSuperLocalBinding\.swift:150](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/e659edc25318b0ba9bcbf95c2755eec8b4a1708f/provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Engine/Bridge/NemotronSuperLocalBinding.swift#L150) · T-041

\`executeBridge\` always submits with \`cacheScope: ""\` and \`cacheEnabled: reusesTextPrefixes\`\. T\-041's account isolation relies on a coordinator\-authored \`cacheSalt\` derived from authenticated account, model build and prompt contract\. Neither \`run\` nor \`runValidatedText\` accepts or forwards a scope\. If an owner builds this binding with \`reusesTextPrefixes: true\`, every caller shares one unscoped cache namespace\. The result is cross\-account prefix reuse and a TTFT oracle, which T\-041 says is closed for cross\-account traffic\. Today the route is unregistered and defaults to cold, so this is latent\. Nothing in the binding prevents a later wiring to coordinator\-routed traffic from silently dropping account scoping\. Fix: take the coordinator\-authored scope as a required parameter, or make the cache\-enabled variant refuse an empty scope\. Document this as a T\-041 detection hint\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5
